The campaign surface — Atlas + live board as one kolu feature

Features·seedling·proposed·JUL 18, 2026

Unify the three coordination artifacts — Atlas notes, the orchestrator's hand-maintained dashboard, and the coming chat bot — into one observed surface: notes carry the plans and reasons (authored), a right-panel Board tab carries the live state (derived from what kolu already watches), and chat mirrors the same board. Nothing is hand-synced because status is never written, only observed.

Why: the scribe problem

Running kolu’s own development as a multi-agent campaign currently uses three disconnected artifacts:

  1. Atlas notes — the plans and reasons (this knowledge base). Correct as authored, durable files.
  2. The orchestrator dashboard — a JSON file (orchestrator-data.js) the coordinator agent hand-writes after every event, rendered by a static HTML skill asset.
  3. The chat bot (pesu, per kolu under any chat app) — planned to render a “who-needs-me board” into a thread.

The dashboard violates kolu’s own philosophy twice. The philosophy says the interface is auto-detected, zero setup — “kolu builds its interface by observing what users already do… rather than requiring configuration” — and that facts like branch/PR/CI status derive from the terminal’s current working directory. The hand-written dashboard is configuration wearing a trench coat: it duplicates state the daemons already observe, so it drifts (the board goes stale, notes disagree with the board, links break when terminals re-key), and keeping it honest required a Stop hook whose only job is to nag the scribe. The disease is that a derived view is hand-authored; every sync pain is a symptom.

The fix is the split the chat-native note already names: observe flows out raw; act flows in through one door. Applied fully:

Layer Carries Authored or observed
Atlas note the plan: phases, design, rationale, post-mortem authored — deliberately, once
Board the state: which lane is where, right now observed — derived at view time, written by no one
Chat thread the same board, socially mirrored — rendered from the board, never a copy

The join needs no configuration because the campaign already follows one naming convention: a lane’s worktree = its branch = its PR, and a design-bearing lane’s branch names its note slug. A convention the coordinator already works by — exactly the shape of “recent repos track cd events”: the system observes what the workflow already does.

Scoping: whose board is this?

The right panel is per-terminal — so what does this terminal’s Board show? The same association the Code tab already uses: the terminal’s cwd names the repo, and the repo is the campaign. cwd → repo root → every worktree of that repo → their terminals, branches, PRs, sensor states.

  • Two terminals in the same repo show the same board (as the Code tab shows them the same files) — the panel is a per-terminal viewport, the content is the repo’s.
  • A terminal in a different repo (drishti) shows that repo’s campaign — multi-project coordination falls out with zero configuration, the “one orchestrator, many projects” shape.
  • A terminal in no repo shows an empty tab, honestly.

No campaign registry, no board picker — the cwd derivation again.

Everything in that mock is already observed by the running system, today:

Element Source (existing)
the lanes kolu’s terminals; each terminal’s cwd names its worktree
the colored dot padi’s agent sensors — working / asking-you / idle (the padi-tui wait buckets)
the sub-line the same sensors’ detail (which agent, what state, how long)
worktree → branch → PR chip the cwd→branch derivation the README names, joined to the forge PR for that branchThe server already derives branch/PR/CI status from a terminal’s cwd for the terminal chrome — the Board reuses that machinery, it does not add a second poller.
CI chip the same PR’s checks
▤ note chip branch name ↔ note slug (the naming convention); links into the Code tab
shipped PRs whose branch had a lane, now merged — an archive nobody curates

Nobody writes any of this. The coordinator dispatching a new lane = creating a worktree and a terminal — which is what makes the lane appear. A PR merging is what flips its chip. An agent finishing is what turns its dot. The board cannot be stale because there is nothing to update.

The note side: phases declared, status resolved

A note keeps owning the structure — what the phases are — but stops hand-stamping outcomes. PrLink (and a small PhasePill) resolve the live PR state at render time in kolu’s Code tab:

Phase tree — agent-spawn-first-class
PR 1 · stop the data loss — #1880 merged
PR 1.5 · the last spawn seam — #1884 merged
PR 2 · detection — #1889 draft · CI running
PR 3 · the face verb — no PR — waits on kolu-tui
pills are live — the note's text never contains an outcome

The note and the board can no longer disagree, because they render the same fact from the same source — one is the plan’s view of it, the other the fleet’s.

The flows

Dispatch. The coordinator (the act door — unchanged) cuts worktree = branch = lane, creates a terminal in it, and briefs the agent. The lane appears on the Board by observation. Zero writes.

Attention. An agent flips to asking-you → its dot turns amber and the who-needs-me strip counts it → the notify seam pings (desktop today; the pesu thread tomorrow — same seam, per the chat-native note). You click the lane → you are in the terminal (the depth kolu owns). Answer, step out.

Reading the plan. Every design-bearing lane shows its ▤ note chip → Code tab opens the note → the note’s phase pills show live outcomes. One click from “what is happening” to “why”.

Shipping. A PR merges (the human merges — unchanged). Its lane’s chip flips to merged; the note’s pill flips identically; the lane retires to shipped when its terminal closes. Nobody announces anything.

Chat. pesu renders this same board into the thread on demand and pings on the attention flow — the “mirror of the coordinator” already specified in the chat-native note. It gains a data source instead of needing one invented.

What stays conversational (deliberately off-board). Gate rulings, CI venue arbitration, box leases — coordinator knowledge with no observable substrate. They live in the dialogue and in notes as decisions, not on the board as state. Putting them on a board is what created the scribe.

What this deletes

  • orchestrator-data.js and the same-turn-update ritual
  • the static dashboard HTML skill asset
  • the board-freshness Stop hook (#1888) — enforcement of a duty that no longer exists
  • hand-stamped statuses inside notes (and their drift)
  • terminal-UUID note links that die on re-key — the Board links notes first-class

Phases

Phase Scope Deletes
P1 — live pills PrLink/PhasePill resolve PR state at render time in the Code tab’s note view (small; client + a cached forge lookup) hand-stamped outcomes in notes
P2 — the Board tab a derived campaign collection on the server (terminals ⋈ worktree ⋈ branch ⋈ PR ⋈ CI ⋈ agent-sensor state — reusing the existing cwd-derivation machinery) + the right-panel tab rendering it the dashboard file, its HTML, hook #1888
P3 — the thread mirror pesu renders the Board + attention pings (the chat-native note’s own plan, now with its data source shipped) nothing — it completes the picture

Philosophy check

Every element must pass the two-principle test: agent-agnostic (the Board watches terminals and forges — it wraps no agent, and a lane running codex or opencode renders identically) and auto-detected, zero setup (if a Board element needs someone to write state for it, it is designed wrong — redesign it to observe, or move it to a note as a decision).
